_why: The household words for a micro zone this site names differently, the same idea as ops/room-also-called.json but at zone scope. Every entry is measured, not guessed: the 'queries' and 'covered' figures are from ops/keyword-demand.json's own harvest. A word earns a place here only if people type it AND this site does not already answer for it.
_rule: Do not add a word with no measured queries, and do not add a word the site already covers. Keyed 'Room|Zone' using the same exact room/zone names as content.json, matching the convention ops/zone-search-terms.json already uses for its own lookup key.

Primary Bedroom|Bed and Bedding Zone.source: ops/keyword-demand-global.json 2026-10-23 (gb, au, in, ca): 'how to organise bedsheets' (rank 2, gap, gb/au/in) and 'how to organize bedsheets' (rank 9, gap, ca), both 0.0 coverage, scored to /about.html via tie-break since no page used the word 'bedsheets'

Kitchen|Lower Cabinet and Cookware Zone.source: ops/keyword-demand-global.json 2026-10-29 (gb, au, in): 'how to organise a kitchen corner cupboard', rank 4, 0.333 coverage, scored to kitchen-deck.html

Kitchen|Upper Cabinet Zone.source: ops/keyword-demand-global.json 2026-10-30 (au): 'how to organise dinnerware', rank 5, 0.0 coverage, scored to /about.html via tie-break since no page used the word 'dinnerware'. Zone purpose ('Light storage at eye level and above for the dishes you reach for every day') and its own straighten pass ('dinner plates and everyday bowls at eye level') confirm the semantic match. Named 'dinnerware cabinet', not the bare word 'dinnerware': 'dinnerware' is the contents, not a name anyone calls this cabinet, and the also-called heading reads as a zone-name synonym ('Also called the X'), so the bare noun alone would misread as a claim nobody calling it that actually makes. 'Dinnerware cabinet' still carries the word the query searches for.
